textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of RNA in action — centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around each structure so labels can attach later. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark-charcoal background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. ABSOLUTE CENTRAL RULE, more important than anything else in this prompt: EVERY RNA STRAND SHOWN MUST BE A SINGLE STRAND — ONE continuous ribbon with bases projecting off ONE side or folding back to touch itself, NEVER two separate strands twisted together into a double helix like a DNA ladder. If you find yourself drawing two parallel backbones spiralling around a shared axis with rungs between them, STOP — that is DNA, and is wrong here. COMPOSITION: a single long wavy mRNA ribbon (cool slate blue-grey #7FA0B8, thin coloured bumps of the four bases along its outer edge: green #6FBF73=A, warm red-orange #D9622B=U, gold #E8B93E=G, blue #3E7FB0=C — never draw base-letter glyphs, colour only) runs diagonally across the frame as ONE unbroken strand, looping back on itself once partway along to form a small HAIRPIN / STEM-LOOP (a short stretch where the SAME strand pairs with itself into a mini double-stranded stem capped by a rounded unpaired loop — this is still one strand folding, not two strands joining). Where the mRNA passes near the centre, paint a small tRNA molecule folded into its unmistakable CLOVERLEAF/L-SHAPE (warm tan-cream ribbon, four looping arms meeting at a central junction, then packed into a compact L): one tip of the L is the ANTICODON LOOP, nestled right up against one specific three-base stretch of the mRNA (the CODON) so the two are clearly pairing; the OPPOSITE tip of the L carries a small distinct coloured bead (the attached amino acid) at the free 3' tail end, clearly separated from the anticodon end. In the lower portion of the frame, paint the knobbly, irregular, membrane-free bulk of a ribosome (large lobe warm terracotta #C24B3E, small lobe cool blue #4E7FB0, exactly matching this atlas's own ribosome house colours, bumpy rRNA-and-protein surface texture, NEVER a smooth sphere) with the mRNA strand threading through the groove between its two subunits. In the upper corner, optionally paint a simple ring shape representing a nuclear pore, with the mRNA strand emerging from it, tying the scene to the nucleus. CRITICAL RULES: every strand segment is single-stranded; the only 'doubled' look anywhere is the SHORT SELF-PAIRED hairpin stem and the tRNA's own folded arms — never a full-length two-independent-strand double helix. No thymine, no 'T' — only the four A/U/G/C base colours, all rendered as colour only, never as letters. No membrane around the mRNA or tRNA. Exactly one of each structure; no duplicated ribosomes or tRNAs. ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT OF ANY KIND anywhere in the image — no letters (including no 'A'/'U'/'G'/'C' glyphs), no numbers, no words, no scale bars, no arrows, no watermarks.

Fill the whole square edge-to-edge with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Subject: one long, gently curving single filament (cool blue-grey false colour) crosses the frame, with small bead-like bumps along it (the bases) and one small tight loop-back partway along (a hairpin). Near the centre, a compact, tightly folded knot of filament sits distinctly apart — a tRNA folded into its characteristic bent/angular L-shape, with one end tucked close against the long strand (the anticodon meeting a codon) and a small distinct bead-like tag standing off the opposite end (the attached amino acid). Nearby, a denser, irregularly knobbly, walnut-like clustered mass (false-coloured in warm coral/terracotta and cool blue lobes, exactly matching this atlas's ribosome reference) represents the RNA-rich bulk of a ribosome, with the long filament threading into a groove in it. Crisp, high-contrast 3D surface relief, shallow depth of field so the far background falls softly out of focus, cool studio microscopy lighting, specimen resting on a subtly textured substrate. CRITICAL: no long two-filament double helix anywhere. No membrane or smooth shell on any structure. Single composition only, no duplicated ribosomes. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks anywhere in the image.
